tasks.title: Teams API: list/filter/search, create, detail, edit, status workflow
tasks.description: Implement src/server/routes/teams.ts per docs/architecture.md § API: GET / (ListTeamsQuery status+q filters, newest first), POST / (201 Team, status Registered, 409 duplicate name case-insensitive via name_key), GET /:id (loadTeamDetail, 404), PATCH /:id (F10, 409 duplicate, own name allowed), POST /:id/status (only MANUAL_NEXT_STATUS[current] allowed else 409; insert kind:'status' update 'Status changed to X' in same transaction). Validate bodies with contract schemas; 400 { error: 'Invalid input', details }. Use helpers in src/server/lib/teams.ts. Tests use app.request against the in-memory DB; use unique team names per test.
acceptance: npm run check passes
tests/unit/teams-api.test.ts: POST valid → 201 with id + status 'Registered'; missing name → 400 {error}; 'sky hackers' after 'Sky Hackers' → 409 'A team with this name already exists'
GET /api/teams?status=Building and ?q=ada (member or team name, case-insensitive) filter and combine
GET /api/teams/:id → TeamDetail parses; unknown id → 404
POST /status: Registered→Building→Submitted ok and adds 'Status changed to Building' update; skip, backwards and 'Judged' → 409 with status unchanged
PATCH renames/edits; duplicate name → 409; status unchanged

tasks.title: Progress updates + judge scoring API

Tests insert fixture teams directly via db + schema (do not depend on teams.ts being implemented).

prd.pitch: A single-screen control room for organizers of a 24-hour hackathon: register teams, move them through Registered → Building → Submitted → Judged, post timestamped progress updates, collect judge scores, and see a live dashboard and leaderboard.
users: Hackathon organizer: registers teams, advances their status, posts progress updates, watches the dashboard (no login).
Judge: opens a submitted team and scores it 1-10 on Innovation, Execution and Demo with an optional comment (same no-login app, entered by an organizer or judge at the laptop).

features.title: Register and list teams
features.story: As an organizer I register a team with a name, member names and a project idea, and see all teams in a list. New teams start as Registered. Team names are unique case-insensitively. Navigation has links labelled Dashboard, Teams, Leaderboard.
acceptance: Given the Teams page (/teams), When I click the button 'Register team', Then a form appears with labelled fields 'Team name', 'Members (comma-separated)', 'Project idea' and a submit button 'Register team'.

Given the form is filled with Team name 'Sky Hackers', Members 'Ana Lee, Raj Patel', Project idea 'Drone-based trail mapping', When I submit, Then the Teams list shows a card 'Sky Hackers' with members 'Ana Lee' and 'Raj Patel', the idea text, and a status badge 'Registered'.

Given an empty 'Team name' or empty Members or empty 'Project idea', When I submit, Then a visible error message appears next to the empty field ('Team name is required', 'Add at least one member', 'Project idea is required') and no team is created.
Given a team named 'Sky Hackers' exists, When I register 'sky hackers', Then the form shows the error 'A team with this name already exists' and the team count is unchanged.
Given the Teams list is empty after filtering, Then an empty state with the text 'No teams match your filters' is shown; Given no teams exist at all, the empty state reads 'No teams registered yet'.
Given the API receives a create-team request with a missing name, Then it responds 400 with { error }; a valid request returns the created team with status 'Registered' and an id.

features.title: Team status workflow
features.story: Each team has exactly one status that moves forward only: Registered → Building → Submitted → Judged. Organizers advance Registered→Building and Building→Submitted from the team detail page (/teams/:id) with one click. Judged is reached only by scoring (F5), never by a button. No backward moves.
acceptance: Given a Registered team's detail page, Then a button 'Move to Building' is visible; When clicked, Then the status badge reads 'Building' and the button now reads 'Move to Submitted'.
Given a Building team, When I click 'Move to Submitted', Then the badge reads 'Submitted' and no advance button is shown (instead the 'Score this team' section from F5 is shown).
Given a Judged team, Then no 'Move to' button is shown.
Given a status change, Then an update entry is automatically added to the team's timeline with text 'Status changed to Building' (or 'Submitted') and a timestamp.
Given the API receives a status change that skips a step (Registered → Submitted) or goes backwards or targets 'Judged' directly, Then it responds 409 with { error } and the status is unchanged.
The status badge on every team card and detail page uses the exact labels 'Registered', 'Building', 'Submitted', 'Judged' with a distinct color per status.

features.title: Timestamped progress updates
features.story: On a team's detail page the organizer posts short progress updates (max 280 characters). They appear newest-first with a timestamp, together with automatic status-change entries.
acceptance: Given a team detail page, Then a labelled textarea 'Progress update' and a button 'Post update' are visible.
Given I type 'Backend API is live' and click 'Post update', Then the text appears at the top of the team's 'Updates' list with a visible timestamp, and the textarea is cleared.
Given an empty or whitespace-only update, When I click 'Post update', Then the error 'Update cannot be empty' is shown and nothing is added.

Given an update longer than 280 characters, When I submit, Then the error 'Update must be 280 characters or fewer' is shown and nothing is added; a character counter such as '12/280' is displayed under the textarea.
Given a team with no updates, Then the Updates list shows the empty state 'No updates yet'.
Given two updates posted in order A then B, Then B is listed above A.
Given the API receives an update for an unknown team id, Then it responds 404 with { error }.

features.title: Dashboard with status counts and latest updates
features.story: The home page (/) shows how many teams are in each status and a feed of the latest updates across all teams, so organizers can see the whole event at a glance.
acceptance: Given the seeded demo data, When I open /, Then four stat tiles show 'Registered 2', 'Building 3', 'Submitted 2', 'Judged 3' (label and number in the same tile) plus a 'Total teams 10' tile.
Given the dashboard, Then a section 'Latest updates' lists the 10 most recent updates across all teams, newest first, each showing team name, update text and timestamp.
Given I click a team name inside the 'Latest updates' feed, Then I navigate to that team's detail page.
Given I post a new update on a team and return to /, Then that update is the first item in 'Latest updates' and the tile counts reflect any status change.

Given the dashboard stays open, Then it refetches data every 5 seconds so updates posted from another browser tab appear without a manual reload (verifiable by posting via API and waiting up to 6 seconds).
Given no updates exist, Then 'Latest updates' shows the empty state 'No updates yet'.

features.title: Judge scoring of submitted teams
features.story: A judge opens a Submitted team and scores it 1-10 on Innovation, Execution and Demo with an optional comment and a required judge name. The first score moves the team to Judged. Multiple judges may score the same team (a Judged team can still receive more scores); the team's average is the mean of all criterion scores across all judges, shown to 2 decimals.
acceptance: Given a team with status Submitted, Then its detail page shows a section 'Score this team' with labelled fields 'Judge name', 'Innovation (1-10)', 'Execution (1-10)', 'Demo (1-10)', 'Comment (optional)' and a button 'Submit score'.
Given a team with status Registered or Building, Then the 'Score this team' section is not shown, and the API rejects a score request with 409 and { error }.

Given Judge name 'Dr. Kim', Innovation 8, Execution 7, Demo 9 and I click 'Submit score', Then the team's badge becomes 'Judged', the page shows 'Average score 8.00' and a 'Scores' list row with 'Dr. Kim', 'Innovation 8', 'Execution 7', 'Demo 9'.

Given any criterion is 0, 11, non-integer or empty, or Judge name is empty, When I submit, Then a visible field error is shown ('Enter a whole number from 1 to 10' / 'Judge name is required') and no score is saved; the API responds 400 with { error, details }.
Given a Judged team scored by Dr. Kim (8,7,9), When a second judge 'Ms. Cho' submits (6,6,6), Then the page shows 'Average score 7.00' and 2 rows in 'Scores'.
Given a comment 'Great demo' is entered, Then it is displayed in that score's row; Given no comment, the row shows no comment text.
Given a Submitted team with no scores, Then the detail page shows 'No scores yet' in the Scores area.

features.title: Leaderboard
features.story: The Leaderboard page (/leaderboard) ranks all Judged teams by average score, highest first, so organizers can announce winners.
acceptance: Given the seeded demo data, When I open /leaderboard, Then a table lists 3 rows in this order with rank, team, average and judge-count columns: 1 'Neural Nomads' 9.00, 2 'Quantum Leapers' 7.67, 3 'Code Ninjas' 6.33.
Given a Submitted team 'Cloud Nine' is scored (10, 10, 10) by one judge, When I reload /leaderboard, Then 'Cloud Nine' is rank 1 with 10.00 and the other teams shift down one rank.
Given two teams with an equal average, Then the one with the earlier first-score time ranks higher and both show consecutive ranks (no shared rank).
Given a team name in the leaderboard, When clicked, Then I navigate to its detail page.
Given no Judged teams exist, Then the empty state 'No judged teams yet' is shown.
Teams that are not Judged never appear on the leaderboard.

features.title: Filter by status and search teams
features.story: On the Teams page organizers filter by status with a control and search by team or member name; both combine.
acceptance: Given /teams, Then a filter control with options 'All', 'Registered', 'Building', 'Submitted', 'Judged' (default 'All') and a search input labelled 'Search teams or members' are visible.
Given the seeded data, When I choose 'Building', Then exactly 3 team cards are shown, all with badge 'Building'.

Given the seeded data, When I type 'ada' into the search, Then only teams having a member whose name contains 'ada' (case-insensitive) or a team name containing 'ada' are shown, including 'Pixel Pioneers' (member Ada Okafor).
Given filter 'Building' and search 'ada', Then only teams satisfying both are shown.
Given a search with no matches, Then the empty state 'No teams match your filters' is shown; clearing the search restores all 10 teams.
Given a dashboard stat tile, When I click it (e.g. 'Submitted'), Then I land on /teams with that status filter pre-selected (URL query ?status=Submitted).

features.title: Realistic demo data
features.story: On first start with an empty database the app seeds 10 teams across all statuses, progress updates and scores so every screen looks alive. Seed only when empty.
acceptance: Given a fresh database, When the app starts, Then /teams lists 10 teams: Registered: 'Data Wranglers', 'Team Rocket'; Building: 'Pixel Pioneers' (members Ada Okafor, Ben Tran, Chloe Ruiz), 'Byte Me', 'Null Pointers'; Submitted: 'Cloud Nine', 'Hack Attack'; Judged: 'Neural Nomads', 'Quantum Leapers', 'Code Ninjas'.
Given the seeded data, Then there are at least 14 progress updates spread over the last 24 hours with distinct timestamps, and every non-Registered team has at least one update.
Given the seeded scores, Then Neural Nomads averages 9.00, Quantum Leapers 7.67 and Code Ninjas 6.33, each scored by one judge.
Given the app restarts with existing data, Then no duplicate teams are created.

features.title: Responsive layout for laptop and phone
features.story: All pages work at 1280px laptop width and at 375px phone width without horizontal scrolling or overlapping controls.
acceptance: Given a 375x667 viewport, When I open /, /teams, a team detail page and /leaderboard, Then document scrollWidth does not exceed the viewport width (no horizontal scroll).
Given a 375px viewport, Then the navigation links Dashboard, Teams, Leaderboard are reachable (visible or behind a button labelled 'Menu').
Given a 375px viewport, Then the stat tiles stack into at most 2 columns and the Teams filter and search inputs are full width.
Given a 1280px viewport, Then the dashboard shows the stat tiles in a single row and 'Latest updates' beside or below without overlap.
Every interactive control has a visible text label and a minimum tap target height of 40px at 375px width.

features.title: Edit team details
features.story: Organizers can fix typos in a team's name, members and project idea from the detail page. Status and scores are untouched.
acceptance: Given a team detail page, When I click 'Edit team', Then the form is prefilled with the current name, members and idea and has buttons 'Save changes' and 'Cancel'.
Given I change the idea to 'New idea' and click 'Save changes', Then the detail page shows 'New idea' and the status and scores are unchanged.
Given I rename the team to another existing team's name, Then the error 'A team with this name already exists' is shown and nothing is saved.

outOfScope: Authentication, accounts, roles or per-judge logins; the app is single organizer-facing with no login. Judge name is a free-text field, not an identity.
Deleting teams, updates or scores; editing or deleting posted updates or scores.
Moving a team backwards in status; manually setting Judged without a score.
Real-time push (WebSockets/SSE): 'live' is implemented by 5-second polling on the dashboard.
File uploads, project links/repo integration, team avatars, email or chat notifications.
Judging rubrics beyond the three fixed criteria (Innovation, Execution, Demo); weighted scores; judge assignments.
Multiple events or hackathons; the app tracks a single event.
Pagination; the app assumes at most ~100 teams.
Tie-breaking beyond earliest first-score time; scores from the same judge name are allowed more than once and all count.
